question.text: An organization having which of the following characteristics pose a VALID social objective per Ch 1.4.2?

answer.text: An enterprise whose primary bottom line is maximising shareholder profit and redistributing it among its board/staff
An organisation created to serve social good, with a social mission, creating social value through social change and building social capital
An organisation focused solely on financial returns but incidentally benefiting society
A for-profit entity whose profit is distributed as dividend to all shareholders

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook p.20, a social objective denotes an entity created to serve social good, with a social mission, creating social value through social change, building social capital and having a social bottom line. Profit-distribution-to-stakeholders is the antithesis of a social objective. The Trap: Options A, C and D all centre profit or dividend — the opposite of a social objective. Option B is the source-backed definition. Note: A genuine social objective is reflected in the entity's purpose, mission and value-creation, not merely incidental social benefit alongside profit-maximisation.
